source_text: What about the features from E-cool-memories?

fragments.text: What about the features from E-cool-memories?

reply_text:
I'll read E-cool-memories and check which of its features exist in the running system.Checking what minus40 exposes, whether it has live data, how the brief's Facts section is meant to read it, and where the Lean side stands.The scratch store on :7093 is listening but its accept queue is full and the live query timed out. Checking its JVM, the hooks that feed it, and the failing m40 test.The store came back at 17:30:58Z and the follower resumed at 17:34Z. Recording the minus40 findings beside this morning's note, then replying.㊥ (gist) The E-cool-memories features are the minus40 (M40°) temporal-memory commands and their Lean checker. All of them work on today's data: a live two-day delta streamed from the store into Lean was accepted a few minutes ago. But the store they read, the scratch futon1b on :7093, had been wedged for the last 14 hours until something restarted it at 17:30Z, and nothing in futon3c or the 象 brief reads minus40 at all. Record: futon3c 56ac45f03, addendum in `LAB-2026-10-14-live-memory-check.md`.

㊬ ("the features") Checked this turn, each against the live store:

| feature | result |
|---|---|
| `m40 net-changed 2026-10-12 2026-10-14` | 26 facts added, 0 removed, 1.4 s |
| `m40 history read-the-clock` | 13 events, including the 10-12 rewrite of my own memory file |
| `export-delta` piped into the Lean trace checker | `M40-DELTA-ACCEPTED 1953→1979`, 3.4 s |
| Lean public fixture | `M40-DELTA-ACCEPTED 2→2`, oleans for all five CoolMemories modules built 10-13 |
| `test_m40.py` | 6 tests pass |

That last Lean line is the P4 receipt reproduced on this week's memories, so it is a live demo you can run from a shell in under five seconds.

㊩ ("can be brought online") The scratch store on :7093 runs with a 1 GB heap in a `systemd-run` scope. From 03:03Z today its accept queue was full and every connection timed out. The ingest hook logged 826 timeouts and advanced no state. The follower's open view froze at 02:55Z. Its liveness port kept answering 200, so no check noticed. A new scope started the store at 17:30:58Z, not from this seat, and the follower resumed at 17:34Z. This is the same failure shape futon1b had on 07-13, and the fix applied there, exit on out-of-memory plus restart on failure, is not on this store's command line.

㊩ ("fully integrated") minus40 is integrated with Claude Code sessions through two hooks, ingest on every tool call and a session-start brief, but the brief is enabled for claude-15 only, so this seat gets none. On the futon3c side there is no integration: no code under `src/`, `emacs/` or `scripts/` references minus40, and the 象 resume brief's Facts section prints a stub saying no minus40 fact was read. The two memory systems share a design and a store engine but do not read each other.

㊭ (three steps, in order) Run the scratch store as a user unit with the out-of-memory exit and restart, and a 2 GB heap, so today's outage cannot recur silently. Enable the session brief for all seats, or at least mine, and watch one week of briefs. Wire the resume brief's Facts section to `m40 asof` over the mission's seats, which is the first place 象 and M40° would actually meet.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I do the first step now? It restarts a scratch store, not the live :7073, and the ingest hook retries anything it missed, so nothing is lost by it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("the basic memory system works") Your message was recorded at 16:12:48Z, read by 象-sonnet 90 s later as `qualify` + `ask-action`, and the prompt header carried three retrieved patterns. The 象 service reports health ok. The frames for this session (54 turns since 10-11) pass five of the six McCarthy checks: ordering, acts named, commits exist, promises accounted, rewind pins. The sixth, "recording is a side effect of acting", fails on 53 of 54 turns, and that failure is the futon1b symptom, not missing replies.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("fully integrated") futon1b heap is 4014 of 4096 MB, old generation at 99.5 %, a full GC roughly once a second. Session-scoped evidence queries answer 504 or hang; the health probe is 3 ms, so zone-health says PASS. In your Emacs the last evidence delivery outcome is `retry`, with 452 such retries since it started on 10-08. The outbox is empty, so the rows did land late, but the turn record only learns its evidence id on an immediate ack. Today 16 of 42 operator records have no evidence link, all typed turns since 13:21Z. The text-search sidecar also reports not reconciled since boot. The unit has no memory ceiling set, and the vitality sampler points at a retired unit, so nothing alarmed.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (one decision) Restart futon1b-zone now? Your 09-08 ruling says futon1b restarts need no quiet time, and the Emacs outbox is the client-side durability that ruling asked for. If the heap pegs again within hours, the working set has outgrown 4 GB and the heap needs raising with a MemoryHigh set under it. I have not touched the JVM.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (two small fixes, if you want them) Record the deterministic evidence id on a `retry` outcome with a delivery state, so a slow store stops costing the link. Point the vitality sampler at `futon1b-zone.service` so heap over 85 % alarms before an operator turn is the first symptom.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("live demos based on my current interactions") All loaded in your running Emacs and checked: `M-x turn-stepper` in this buffer steps SAID / PARSE / PATTERNS / HAPPENED over this session's 54 turns. `M-x xiang-resume-brief` renders the M-象-2000 brief; its `--since` crashed on a bare date and is fixed (6343241a3). `C-c s o` is the session overview. feed.html shows operator turns only. The brief's "awaiting other agents" still lists 59 Zai requisitions that bellbacks closed, the false-open problem on the brief side.
